effect: Win every normal set at once (stage clear; not boss sets)
note: GameShark: the three enemy object pages' state bytes $C100/$C200/$C300 forced to 0, so $01:487E sees all enemies gone and the set ends won ($C590 = 2). With the invincibility code: 6 sets won and 1-1 to 1-4 in 6,000 frames; boss sets don't end with it (the 1-boss waits; $01:48C7 needs the boss itself, $C3F7 = 1). GB1 has no lives: a lost match goes to the continue screen. Game Genie: $01:488A OR A -> XOR A, so the enemy check sees every page empty; with C98-37B-D5D: 12 sets won, 1-1 to 1-4 in 6,000 frames (jp and wario). Mesen 2, Bomberman Collection through its menu, the Japanese code: with C98-37B-D5D and a 6,000-frame bot: 5 sets won, to 1-4, with the GameShark codes; 11 sets won with Game Genie AF8-8AB-3B4.

code: Win 240 rounds of the extra battle (5656; Wario Blast 6565 as Wario)
effect: PERFECT! ENEMY 240 screen with a fixed CODE -SVJV-, then CONGRATULATIONS!
note: After each round the extra battle ($00:35A4) calls $0A:4EFC (Wario $0A:5398), which checks the defeat count $C1D1-$C1D3 (one decimal digit per byte); at 240 it jumps to $0A:4DFF (Wario $0A:528B), which draws PERFECT! / ENEMY 240 / CODE -SVJV- / CONGRATULATIONS! (tile map $08:40D2); A or Start goes back to the title. The code is the same in both carts, likely a contest proof code. In Mesen (JP): the count set to 239 during the battle, one more round won, and the screen came up. Static: Bomberman Collection carries Bomberman GB (Japan)'s 16 banks byte-identical (banks 32-47), including the check at $0A:4EFC and the screen at $0A:4DFF; 5656 is accepted there.

effect: The extra battle's 240-win PERFECT! screen at once (turn on after the 5656 / 6565 code is accepted)
note: GameShark: the defeat count $C1D1-$C1D3 held at 2-4-x, so the first check after a round sees 240+. $C1D1-$C1D3 is also the password digit buffer, so switch the codes on only after the password is accepted, then press A on the GREAT BATTLE intro. Tested in Mesen on both carts. Static (RAM codes): Bomberman Collection carries Bomberman GB (Japan)'s banks byte-identical, so $C1D1-$C1D3 and the check are the same.

effect: Japan plays the attract story after about 36 seconds; Wario Blast stays on the title
note: Japan's title loop counts BC = $3C20 down ($0A:40A7-$40B7) and then jumps to the story ($0A:4106). Wario Blast's loop ($0A:40AA-$40E1) has no counter, as the story is gone. In Mesen with no input: Japan showed the story 36 s after the title, Wario Blast was still on the title at 56 s. Image: Japan (top) and Wario Blast at the title, +36 s and +56 s.

effect: Two tunes the game never plays
note: Music goes through the request byte $C3F1 (CALL $0AC4). The game asks for 00-06 and 0B as constants and 09-12 from the stage table at $00:1F04 (Wario $1E99). The song table at $07:4A0E has 00-12, and 07 and 08 have channel data of their own but no request. 07 is about 11 s, loud, and doesn't loop; 08 is about 11 s, quiet and rhythmic, and doesn't loop either. Recorded in BizHawk. Static: Bomberman Collection carries Bomberman GB (Japan)'s banks byte-identical, so the requests and the song table are the same.

effect: Nine sound effects the game never plays
note: Effects go through CALL $0AE1 with the ID in $C3F1. None of the 70 or so calls asks for 06, 0E or 13-18; 11 is used in Wario Blast only. Each plays when swapped into the title cursor's sound: short blips of 0.2 to 0.7 s, 0E about 1.4 s, 18 nearly 3 s of high noise. Recorded in Mesen. Static: Bomberman Collection carries Bomberman GB (Japan)'s banks byte-identical, so the effect calls and data are the same.

effect: The clock stays at 199 (it jumps there on its first tick)
note: Game Genie: $00:0A5B LD (HL),A (77) -> NOP in the BCD subtract ($00:0A4B) that takes 001 off the clock digits $C585-$C587; only digits that borrow are written (the borrow branch has its own store), so 100 becomes 199 and later ticks change nothing. Only the clock calls this routine. Same address in JP. BizHawk: US and JP: in round 1-1, $C585-7 every 120 frames: 100,099,098,097... without; 100,199,199,199... with; the HUD shows TIME 199. GameShark: US and JP: the clock digits stayed 100 over 960 / 600 frames. Mesen 2, Bomberman Collection through its menu, the Japanese code: clock 199 199 199 199 199 every 120 frames (099 -> 096 without); GameShark 010185C5 + 010086C5 + 010087C5 held 100.

effect: Each set starts with 300 on the clock, about 10 minutes
note: Game Genie: US $00:1F87 / JP $00:1FF2, operand of LD A,$01 that sets the clock's start hundreds digit ($C582, copied to $C585) -> $03. BizHawk: US: clock 300, 299 (100, 099 without). JP: 299, 298, 297 read after the first tick. Mesen 2, Bomberman Collection through its menu, the Japanese code: 03F-F2E-E6E: clock 299, 298, 297.

effect: Up to 7 bombs instead of 4, for every bomber; an 8th bomb-up drops you back to 4
note: Game Genie: US $01:53F1 / JP $01:53E2, operand of CP $04 after the INC of the bomb count (+$2C) -> $08. The following LD (HL),$04 is unchanged, so reaching 8 is clamped to 4.
